title: Base change for pushforward tensored with a bounded-below complex of finite tor amplitude
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $n\ge1$ an integer invertible in $K$.
Consider a commutative diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X&\xleftarrow{\;p\;}&X'&\xleftarrow{\;h\;}&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f'}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle e}\\
\Spec(K)&\longleftarrow&S'&\xleftarrow{\;g\;}&T
\end{array}
$$

of schemes with $X'=X\times_{\Spec(K)}S'$ and
$Y=X'\times_{S'}T$ and with $g$ quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. The canonical map

$$
p^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}(f')^{-1}Rg_*F
\longrightarrow
Rh_*\bigl(h^{-1}p^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}e^{-1}F\bigr)
$$

(adjoint to the map
$h^{-1}p^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}e^{-1}g^{-1}Rg_*F\to h^{-1}p^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}e^{-1}F$
induced by the counit of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]) is an
isomorphism for every $E\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},\kunZn)$ of
tor amplitude in $[a,\infty)$ for
some $a\in\mathbf Z$ and every $F\in\Dplus(T_{\Et},\kunZn)$.
(*Source:* Stacks Project, Tag
[0F1J](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1J).)

proof.text: Put $R=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$ and denote the two functors of the statement by $A(E,F)$ and $B(E,F)$, with comparison $\alpha_{E,F}$. All module categories and sites are taken in a fixed larger universe, so the filtered diagrams below are small. Inverse image of constant-coefficient module sheaves is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and its derived functor is the termwise functor by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. Derived tensor is triangulated in each variable by [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated], and right derived direct image is triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Consequently $A$ and $B$ are triangulated in each variable; the counit formula in the statement makes $\alpha$ a natural transformation compatible with shifts and with the triangles obtained from short exact sequences of complexes. The inverse-image tensor identifications used here are [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal]. Right direct image preserves a lower cohomological bound: apply [lem-kun-tensor-t-est] to underlying abelian sheaves and then [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients](2) to identify the module direct image. We will use this lower bound only for right direct image, never for the derived tensor of two arbitrary cohomologically bounded-below objects. If $n=1$, both coefficient module categories are zero and the assertion follows immediately.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, first two reduction paragraphs; functorial setup

proof.text: By [lem-kun-0f1m] choose a K-flat flat-term model $\mathcal E^\bullet$ for $E$, zero below $a$, whose termwise pullbacks are again K-flat and flat-term. Choose $b$ with $F\in D^{\ge b}$. For $N\ge a$ put $E_N=\sigma_{\le N}\mathcal E$ and $T_N=\sigma_{\ge N+1}\mathcal E$ [def-kun-truncations]. The degreewise split exact sequence $0\to T_N\to\mathcal E\to E_N\to0$ gives a distinguished triangle by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. The bounded flat complex $E_N$ is K-flat by [lem-kun-kflat-criteria](1), as are all its pullbacks. The tails $T_N$ and their pullbacks are K-flat too: tensor the split sequence with any acyclic complex; it stays degreewise split exact after totalization, and its middle and last terms are acyclic, so its first term is acyclic by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. Now represent $F$ and $Rg_*F$ by complexes zero below $b$ using [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. The K-flat tail computes each tensor in $A(T_N,F)$ and inside $B(T_N,F)$ by [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Their total tensor complexes are zero below $N+1+b$; the lower bound from Step 1 gives the same bound after $Rh_*$. Thus in every degree $q<N+b$ the triangle identifies the map $H^q(\alpha_{E,F})$ with $H^q(\alpha_{E_N,F})$: both $H^q$ and $H^{q+1}$ of the tail images vanish. For each fixed $q$ choose $N$ large enough. The bounded complex $E_N$ is a finite extension of shifts of its individual flat terms, using the same stupid-truncation short exact sequences and triangles. It therefore suffices to prove the assertion for a single flat $R$-module sheaf $\mathcal E$ in degree zero. The argument establishes the assertion degree by degree; it does not assume convergence of an infinite filtration.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, first reduction paragraph; the omitted truncation bounds and K-flatness of the tails are written out

proof.text: Fix the flat sheaf $\mathcal E$. The complex $\mathcal E[0]$ is K-flat by [lem-kun-kflat-criteria](1), so its inverse images are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback], applied to this one-term flat complex. Tensor by any of them is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], hence commutes with cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Choose a representative $I$ of $F$ zero below $b$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Set $J_M=\tau_{\le M}I$ [def-kun-truncations], a bounded complex, and $C_M=I/J_M$. This quotient complex is zero below $M$ (its degree-$M$ term is $I^M/\ker d^M$); in particular its cohomology vanishes below $M$. The exact sequence $0\to J_M\to I\to C_M\to0$ gives a triangle by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Exactness of tensor with the inverse images of $\mathcal E$ and the lower direct-image bound of Step 1 put $A(\mathcal E,C_M)$ and $B(\mathcal E,C_M)$ in $D^{\ge M}$. For $q<M-1$ the triangle therefore identifies the comparison for $F$ in degree $q$ with that for $J_M$. Finally the bounded complex $J_M$ is a finite extension of shifts of its individual sheaf terms, by its stupid-truncation exact sequences. It suffices to prove $\alpha_{\mathcal E,\mathcal F}$ for every single sheaf $\mathcal F$; no bounded complex of flat sheaves representing $F$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, second reduction paragraph, reduction of F

proof.text: Induct on a positive divisor $m$ of $n$ annihilating $\mathcal F$. For $m=1$ the sheaf is zero. If $m$ is not prime, choose a prime $\ell\mid m$ and use $0\to\mathcal F[\ell]\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal F[\ell]\to0$. The first term is killed by $\ell$, and the last by $m/\ell$: for a local section $x$, $\ell((m/\ell)x)=mx=0$, so $(m/\ell)x\in\mathcal F[\ell]$. Both annihilators are smaller than $m$. The associated triangle and Step 1 reduce to prime torsion. When $\ell\mathcal F=0$, [lem-kun-0f1j-prime-torsion-coefficient-reduction] identifies this comparison with the restriction of the $k_\ell=\mathbf F_\ell$ comparison for $(\mathcal E/\ell\mathcal E,\mathcal F)$, with the first factor flat. Restriction of coefficients is conservative because it leaves underlying cohomology sheaves unchanged. We can therefore prove the remaining sheaf case over $k_\ell$. The prime $\ell$ is invertible in $K$, since it divides $n$.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, prime-torsion reduction and coefficient identity

proof.text: The arbitrary-scheme untensored base-change lemma [lem-kun-0f1j-arbitrary-scheme-untensored-base-change] applies to the present $\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and to every $K$-scheme $Z$: the prime $\ell$ is invertible in $K$ (Step 4) and $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. It supplies the untensored comparison $(f')^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F\to Rh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$ for the square $Z\times_KS'\leftarrow (Z\times_KS')\times_{S'}T$ over $S'\leftarrow T$, used in the finite-pushforward reduction of Step 8, with no finite-type assumption on $Z$.

source.place: Tags 0F1I and 0EZT, arbitrary-scheme extension in the proof of Tag 0F1J

proof.text:
For $k_\ell$-sheaves $M$ on $X$ define
$$A^q(M)=p^{-1}M\otimes_{k_\ell}(f')^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F,\qquad B^q(M)=R^qh_*(h^{-1}p^{-1}M\otimes_{k_\ell}e^{-1}\mathcal F).$$
Every $k_\ell$-module sheaf is flat: on geometric stalks tensor is ordinary vector-space tensor [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar], which preserves short exact sequences; stalks are exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and detect isomorphisms [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Exactness and conservativity on module sheaves follow by forgetting coefficients [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1). Hence exact tensor and inverse image commute with cohomology [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], and the degree-$q$ map of $\alpha_{M,\mathcal F}$ is a natural map $a^q_M:A^q(M)\to B^q(M)$. Each $A^q$ is an exact functor of $M$. The $B^q$ have the long exact sequences obtained by applying $Rh_*$ to the short exact sequence after the exact functor $M\mapsto h^{-1}p^{-1}M\otimes e^{-1}\mathcal F$; the required distinguished triangle is [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], and $Rh_*$ is triangulated as in Step 1. All the $a^q$ commute with the maps in these sequences by the functorial counit construction. Negative degrees on both sides vanish.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, vector-space paragraph, cohomological comparison and exact functors

proof.text: For an open $U\subseteq X$, the open $U\times_KS'\subseteq X'$ and its preimage in $Y$ form the same diagram for $U$; restriction to them commutes with $Rh_*$ by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction] (with the finite ring $k_\ell$) and with inverse images and tensor products, so the comparison restricts to the comparison for $U$. Isomorphy of a map of sheaves is local, so assume $X$ affine. It is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Use [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaf-colimit-constructible], with the finite ring $k_\ell$, to write any $M$ as a small filtered colimit of constructible $k_\ell$-sheaves $M_i$. Inverse images preserve this colimit because they are left adjoints [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact; lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Tensor preserves it by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]. Finally $h$ is qcqs as a base change of $g$ [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), so its higher direct images preserve these torsion filtered colimits by [lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit]. Forgetting module coefficients commutes with colimits [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] and with higher direct images [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]. Consequently $a^q_M=\varinjlim_i a^q_{M_i}$. These filtered colimits are exact by [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor]. It is enough to prove injectivity, or surjectivity, of $a^q$ on constructible $M$ to obtain it on all $M$. This uses the qcqs constructible-generation node, not the narrower finite-type node lem-kun-03sa.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, vector-space paragraph; Tags 03SA (lemma-torsion-colimit-constructible) and 09Z1 (lemma-relative-colimit)

proof.text: For a constructible $M$ on affine $X$, [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-finite-pushforward-embedding] gives a monomorphism $M\hookrightarrow P=\bigoplus_i\pi_{i,*}\underline{V_i}$ for finitely many finite maps $\pi_i$ and finite $k_\ell$-modules $V_i$. Choose a finite basis of each $V_i$; its constant sheaf is a finite direct sum of $\underline{k_\ell}$. For each resulting summand, [lem-kun-0f1j-finite-pushforward-comparison] identifies the canonical comparison with $\pi'_{i,*}$ of the untensored comparison for $X_i$. That upper square is the product square $X_i\times_K S'$ and $X_i\times_K T$, so Step 5 applies and makes its comparison invertible. Finite additivity gives an isomorphism for $P$ in every degree. No finite-type assumption on $X_i$ or constructibility assertion about the cokernel is used.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, constructible embedding and final finite-pushforward calculation

proof.text: Here are the omitted dimension-shifting details. First fix any $q\ge0$. For every constructible $M$, choose $M\hookrightarrow P$ as in Step 8. If a local section of $A^q(M)$ maps to zero under $a^q_M$, its image in $A^q(P)$ maps to zero under the isomorphism $a^q_P$, and hence is zero. Exactness of $A^q$ makes $A^q(M)\to A^q(P)$ monic, so the original section is zero. This proves injectivity for constructible $M$, and Step 7 proves it for every sheaf $M$, in every degree. Now prove surjectivity for all $M$ by induction on $q$. It suffices at each degree to handle constructible $M$, by Step 7. Write $0\to M\to P\to C\to0$; $C$ may be any sheaf. For $q=0$, $B^0(M)\to B^0(P)$ is monic by left exactness. For $q>0$, induction gives that $a^{q-1}_C$ is surjective, and the map $A^{q-1}(P)\to A^{q-1}(C)$ is surjective by exactness of $A^{q-1}$. Together with the isomorphism $a^{q-1}_P$, these imply that $B^{q-1}(P)\to B^{q-1}(C)$ is surjective. The long exact sequence from Step 6 then makes $B^q(M)\to B^q(P)$ monic as well. Given a local section $b\in B^q(M)$, its image in $B^q(P)$ comes from $a\in A^q(P)$ by Step 8. The image of $a$ in $A^q(C)$ has zero image under $a^q_C$, since the composite $B^q(M)\to B^q(P)\to B^q(C)$ is zero. Injectivity already proved for arbitrary $C$ forces that image to vanish. Exactness gives, locally, a lift $a_M\in A^q(M)$ of $a$. The images of $a^q_M(a_M)$ and $b$ in $B^q(P)$ coincide; monicity of $B^q(M)\to B^q(P)$ makes them equal. This proves surjectivity. All lifting statements here are local on an etale test object, as appropriate for exactness of sheaves. Therefore every $a^q_M$ is an isomorphism. This is a diagram chase using the exact sequences established in Steps 6–8; no extra effacement theorem or constructibility of $C$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, dimension shifting (details omitted in the source, expanded here)

proof.text: Step 9 proves the comparison for two sheaves over $k_\ell$ in all nonnegative cohomological degrees, and the negative degrees vanish by Step 6. A derived morphism inducing cohomology isomorphisms is invertible: after forgetting coefficients use [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] (the induced stalk maps are isomorphisms), and reflect isomorphisms back by the conservative coefficient-forgetting functor of [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison]. The prime-torsion induction in Step 4 now proves the assertion for a flat $R$-sheaf $\mathcal E$ and an arbitrary $R$-sheaf $\mathcal F$; Step 3 gives every bounded-below $F$; Step 2 gives the original $E$ of lower tor amplitude. At every reduction it was the natural counit-defined comparison that was compared, so the resulting isomorphism is the canonical map of the statement.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $n\ge1$ an integer invertible in $K$.
Consider a commutative diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X&\xleftarrow{\;p\;}&X'&\xleftarrow{\;h\;}&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f'}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle e}\\
\Spec(K)&\longleftarrow&S'&\xleftarrow{\;g\;}&T
\end{array}
$$

of schemes with $X'=X\times_{\Spec(K)}S'$ and
$Y=X'\times_{S'}T$ and with $g$ quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. The canonical map

$$
p^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}(f')^{-1}Rg_*F
\longrightarrow
Rh_*\bigl(h^{-1}p^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}e^{-1}F\bigr)
$$

(adjoint to the map
$h^{-1}p^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}e^{-1}g^{-1}Rg_*F\to h^{-1}p^{-1}E\kunotimes{\kunZn}e^{-1}F$
induced by the counit of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]) is an
isomorphism for every $E\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},\kunZn)$ of
tor amplitude in $[a,\infty)$ for
some $a\in\mathbf Z$ and every $F\in\Dplus(T_{\Et},\kunZn)$.

proof.text:
*Reduction to a single flat module.* By [lem-kun-0f1m]
(the tor-amplitude criterion of [def-kun-tor-amplitude]) we may
represent $E$ by a bounded-below K-flat complex
$\mathcal E^\bullet$ of flat $\kunZn$-module sheaves, with
$\mathcal E^i=0$ for $i<a$. Choose an integer $b$ such that
$\mathcal H^i(F)=0$ for $i<b$. Choose a large integer $N$ and
consider the short exact sequence

$$
0\to\sigma_{\ge N+1}\mathcal E^\bullet\to\mathcal E^\bullet\to
\sigma_{\le N}\mathcal E^\bullet\to0
$$

of stupid truncations ([def-kun-truncations]). This produces a
distinguished triangle $E''\to E\to E'\to E''[1]$ in
$D(X_{\Et},\kunZn)$. For fixed $F$, both sides of the arrow in
the statement of the lemma are triangulated functors in $E$
([lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated],
[def-kun-derived-tensor],
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image]). By
[lem-kun-derived-tensor-t-est] (and
[lem-kun-tensor-t-est] for the right hand side), the objects

$$
p^{-1}E''\kunotimes{\kunZn}(f')^{-1}Rg_*F
\quad\text{and}\quad
Rh_*\bigl(h^{-1}p^{-1}E''\kunotimes{\kunZn}e^{-1}F\bigr)
$$

are sitting in degrees $\ge N+b$. Hence, if we can prove the lemma
for the object $E'$, then comparing the two distinguished triangles
(five lemma on the long exact cohomology sequences) shows that the
lemma holds for $E$ in degrees $\le N+b$, and letting
$N\to\infty$ we conclude. Thus we may assume $E$ is represented
by a bounded complex of flat $\kunZn$-module sheaves. Doing another
argument of the same nature (decomposing the bounded complex through
its stupid truncation triangles, using that both sides are
triangulated functors in $E$), we may assume $E$ is given by a
single flat $\kunZn$-module sheaf $\mathcal E$.

*Reduction of $F$.* Next, we use the same arguments for the
variable $F$ to reduce to the case where $F$ is given by a single
sheaf of $\kunZn$-modules $\mathcal F$: truncate $F$ with
$\tau_{\le M}$ ([def-kun-truncations]) and compare degrees,
then represent the bounded complex $\tau_{\le M}F$ by a bounded
complex and split it into its single sheaves through stupid
truncation triangles.

*Reduction to prime torsion.* Say $\mathcal F$ is annihilated
by an integer $m\mid n$. If $\ell$ is a prime number dividing
$m$ and $m>\ell$, then we can look at the short exact sequence
$0\to\mathcal F[\ell]\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal F[\ell]\to0$
and reduce to smaller $m$ (both sides of the asserted map are
triangulated functors in $F$, and $\mathcal F[\ell]$ is
annihilated by $\ell$ while $\mathcal F/\mathcal F[\ell]$ is
annihilated by $m/\ell$). This finally reduces us to the case
where $\mathcal F$ is annihilated by a prime $\ell\mid n$,
i.e. $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of $\kunFl$-vector spaces. In this
case observe that

$$
p^{-1}\mathcal E\kunotimes{\kunZn}(f')^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F
\;\cong\;
p^{-1}(\mathcal E/\ell\mathcal E)\kunotimes{\kunFl}
(f')^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F
$$

by the flatness of $\mathcal E$ and
[lem-kun-change-of-rings-tensor], and similarly for the other
term. This reduces us to the case where we work with sheaves of
$\kunFl$-vector spaces, which we now discuss.

*The $\kunFl$-vector space case.* Assume $\ell$ is a prime
invertible in $K$ and $\mathcal E$, $\mathcal F$ are sheaves of
$\kunFl$-vector spaces on $X_{\Et}$ and $T_{\Et}$. We want to
show that

$$
p^{-1}\mathcal E\kunotimes{\kunFl}(f')^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F
\longrightarrow
R^qh_*\bigl(h^{-1}p^{-1}\mathcal E\kunotimes{\kunFl}e^{-1}\mathcal F\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$ (the map induced on $\mathcal H^q$ by the asserted map, see [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] and
[lem-kun-bc-base-change]; the tensor product is underived
because $\kunFl$-vector spaces are flat).

This question is local on $X$ ([lem-kun-stalk-faithful-derived]),
hence we may assume $X$ is affine. We can write
$\mathcal E$ as a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves of
$\kunFl$-vector spaces on $X_{\Et}$
([lem-kun-03sa], with the Noetherian ring
$\Lambda=\kunFl$). Since tensor products commute with filtered
colimits and since higher direct images do too
([lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit]), we may assume
$\mathcal E$ is a constructible sheaf of $\kunFl$-vector spaces
on $X_{\Et}$. Then [lemma-weil-pbc-constructible-finite-pushforward],
with $\Lambda=\kunFl$, gives an integer $m$, finite and finitely
presented morphisms $\pi_i:X_i\to X$, and a monomorphism

$$
\mathcal E\longrightarrow P:=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\pi_{i,*}\underline{\kunFl}.
$$

Each summand is constructible by
[lem-kun-095r] and [lem-kun-constant-constructible]; hence
$P$ and the cokernel of $\mathcal E\to P$ are constructible by
[thm-constructible-serre]. We first prove the assertion for each
$\pi_{i,*}\underline{\kunFl}$; finite additivity gives it for
$P$, after which the dimension-shifting argument recovers the
assertion for $\mathcal E$.

To prove this case we extend the diagram of the lemma to

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X_i&\longleftarrow&X'_i&\longleftarrow&Y_i\\
\Big\uparrow{\scriptstyle \pi_i}&&\Big\uparrow{\scriptstyle \pi'_i}&&\Big\uparrow{\scriptstyle \rho_i}\\
X&\longleftarrow&X'&\longleftarrow&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f'}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle e}\\
\Spec(K)&\longleftarrow&S'&\xleftarrow{\;g\;}&T
\end{array}
$$

with all squares cartesian (so $X'_i=X_i\times_XX'$ and
$Y_i=X'_i\times_{X'}Y$; here $\rho_i:Y_i\to Y$ and the unlabelled
maps are the projections). In the equations below we use that
$R\pi_{i,*}=\pi_{i,*}$ and similarly for $\pi'_i$ and $\rho_i$
(finite morphisms, [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]);
we use the Leray spectral sequence through the finite morphisms
([lem-kun-leray-finite]); we use
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] and [lem-kun-0f0g] (the
projection formula, almost trivial for finite morphisms) for
$\pi_i$, $\pi'_i$, $\rho_i$. Doing so we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}
&p^{-1}\pi_{i,*}\underline{\kunFl}\kunotimes{\kunFl}
(f')^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\\
&\qquad=\pi'_{i,*}\underline{\kunFl}\kunotimes{\kunFl}
(f')^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\bigr)\qquad(\text{\Cref{lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange}})\\
&\qquad=\pi'_{i,*}\bigl((\pi'_i)^{-1}(f')^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\bigr)
\qquad(\text{\Cref{lem-kun-0f0g}}).
\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&R^qh_*\bigl(h^{-1}p^{-1}\pi_{i,*}\underline{\kunFl}
\kunotimes{\kunFl}e^{-1}\mathcal F\bigr)\\
&\qquad=R^qh_*\bigl(\rho_{i,*}\underline{\kunFl}
\kunotimes{\kunFl}e^{-1}\mathcal F\bigr)
\qquad(\text{\Cref{lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange}})\\
&\qquad=R^qh_*\bigl(\rho_{i,*}\rho_i^{-1}e^{-1}\mathcal F\bigr)
\qquad(\text{\Cref{lem-kun-0f0g}})\\
&\qquad=\pi'_{i,*}R^qh_{i,*}\rho_i^{-1}e^{-1}\mathcal F
\qquad(\text{\Cref{lem-kun-leray-finite}}).
\end{aligned}
$$

Since
$R^qh_{i,*}\rho_i^{-1}e^{-1}\mathcal F=(\pi'_i)^{-1}(f')^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F$
by [lem-kun-0f1i] (applied to the upper square, with base
scheme $X_i$ of finite type over $K$ and the sheaf
$\mathcal F$, a sheaf of $\kunFl$-vector spaces whose stalks are
$\ell$-torsion with $\ell\mid n$
invertible in $K$, hence of orders invertible in $K$ by
[lem-kun-zn-sheaf-invertible-orders]), we conclude by
[lem-kun-proj-formula-natural], which identifies the asserted
map with the identity under the displayed isomorphisms.
